task_title: Correct README GitReins paragraph that cites nonexistent .gitreins/config.yaml key test_command
task_criteria: 1) grep -n test_command README.md shows no citation of a nonexistent key, or config defines it; 2) paragraph still explains why PATH ordering is irrelevant using the real config mechanism (guards.tests/go.tests/guards.test_mode); 3) brief pastes the .gitreins/config.yaml excerpt backing the sentence.

items.criterion: 1) grep -n test_command README.md shows no citation of a nonexistent key, or config defines it; 2) paragraph still explains why PATH ordering is irrelevant using the real config mechanism (guards.tests/go.tests/guards.test_mode); 3) brief pastes the .gitreins/config.yaml excerpt backing the sentence.
items.detail: All three clauses verified. (1) `grep -n test_command README.md` -> exit=1, no output; `grep -c test_command README.md` -> 0. Same at HEAD: `git show HEAD:README.md | grep -n test_command` -> exit=1. The config does not define the key either (`grep -nE "command|cmd|script|exec" .gitreins/config.yaml` -> exit=1), so removing the citation (rather than adding the key) is the correct resolution. Landed as commit fae0c767, merged at HEAD 22cadb29; the diff deletes the old sentence "The tests lane is interpreter-pinned in `.gitreins/config.yaml` (`test_command`), so PATH ordering is irrelevant." (2) README.md:577-585 now explains PATH ordering via exactly the keys the task named: "`guards.test_mode: full`, the generic `guards.tests` leg is off and `guards.go.tests: true` (with `guards.go.build: true`) is the lane that actually executes." Cross-checked against .gitreins/config.yaml:4 `tests: false`, :5 `test_mode: full`, :26 `build: true`, :35 `tests: true` (under `go:` at :25). Live confirmation: `gitreins guard` -> exit 0, "Tier 1: DEGRADED PASS (skips: go_build=No Go files staged, go_tests=No Go files staged)  (test mode: full)". (3) The config excerpt backing the sentence is pasted inline in the paragraph itself (key names plus values), and its strongest claim — "The file has no command override of any kind" — is verified by the grep exit=1 above. The guard's built-in invocation is confirmed at engine/guards.py:573 -> `["go","test","-count=1","-short","./..."]`, matching README.md:593's table entry `go test -short -count=1 ./...` (same flags, order differs, semantically identical). Note: the task's premise that `test_command` is "nonexistent" holds only for this repo's config — in gitreins 0.21.0 `guards.test_command` is a real honoured key (guard_manager.py:3786, guards.py:551-575) — but the README's new wording is careful and stays accurate by saying "The file has no command override of any kind" rather than "the key does not exist"; verified empirically via `_resolve_go_test_argv(None)` -> built-in argv vs `_resolve_go_test_argv("go test -race ./...")` -> configured string. [resolution 0.14; README.md]
